marks.gloss_en: Shmuel ruled on rider and leader -- one acquires, one does not; which is which was lost in transmission
does the rider (who grasps the animal) prevail over the leader (who makes it walk)?
in Shmuel's text of the kilayim mishna it is the RABBIS who exempt the wagon-sitter (the printed text gives that to R' Meir)
holding the reins of an ownerless animal does not acquire it
Rav Huna: reins acquire when handed over by a fellow person; for a find or a convert's estate they acquire nothing
(entertained) our mishna (rider and leader both acquire) must be the Rabbis -- so a rider acquires
deflection: the mishna's 'rider' also drives the animal with his feet -- a second kind of leading
first tanna: pulling a camel or driving a donkey (or one pulling and one driving) acquires -- 'in this manner'
